result.headline: BMS under-voltage protection opened contactors; SOC was overstated by about 56 pp until an abrupt correction, so the upstream cause is unresolved.
result.explanation: HV loss was the BMS under-voltage protection acting. Upstream, SOC estimation error, low usable capacity and current under-reading all fit the recording equally. This data cannot separate them; documents or independent measurements are needed.

evidence.quote: CHANGE battery.soc[bms] at t=1698.5 s: 45.2 -> 30.8 % (step -14.4, 9x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: The SOC fell by tens of points in about 29 s (56.8 -> 24.0 %) while the current stayed at 6.95 A. Measured charge explains only 0.056 pp.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT battery.pack_current held 6.95 from t=0 to 2100 s (4201 samples)
evidence.shows: The current is a flat 6.95 A for the whole run. Before the correction SOC followed measured charge (ratio 1.036 and 1.291), so the estimator was only counting charge.
The contactors opened at the same instant as fault level 3 (lines 19-20). Level 1 (t=1453) and level 2 (t=1799) came earlier, so the opening is the protective response.

evidence.quote: SHIFT battery.cell_voltage[min] changed level for good at t=640 s: median 3.2 before, 2.864 after V (2240x its variation before)
evidence.shows: The whole pack fell steadily; the highest cell fell too (line 23). This points to a pack-wide shortfall, not one weak cell.

checked.result: One SOC correction of 32.74 pp is unexplained by measured charge. Outside it, SOC tracked counted charge. Delivering the drop would need about 4065 A against the measured 6.95 A.
checked.about: SOC estimation error, usable capacity and current under-measurement together, not any one of them

checked.result: SOC median fell from 57.2 to 23.6 %. Current stayed at 6.95 A with spread 0. Cell max went 2.967 -> 2.941 V and cell min 2.779 -> 2.743 V, a small change next to the SOC drop.
checked.about: The SOC correction as an estimator re-statement; the current did not change

checked.result: There is no step at 640 s: cell and pack voltages and SOC are unchanged across it (level_change_z 0 to 4.0). The SHIFT lines are a slow decline, not an event.
checked.about: A discrete event at 640 s, which is not supported

checked.result: SOC left baseline first (1688.5), then cell max (1782), pack voltage (1787.5) and cell min (1796.5). Level 2 followed at 1799 and the trip at 2100.5. SOC fell first and the voltage alarms came later.
checked.about: The SOC error as the earliest sign; the protection and contactor opening are effects

checked.result: Shortfall of about 56 pp: either SOC overstated, or capacity about 7 Ah, or current under-read about 14.9x. B and C alone need very large errors. A weak cell is insufficient alone because the highest cell also fell 450 mV.
checked.about: Separating the SOC, capacity and current explanations

checked.result: The telemetry cannot separate the three upstream causes. DOC-BMS-HISTORY ranks first because it settled the same finding in an earlier verified case (SOC drift, confirmed). That case is context, not proof here.

effects.why: The contactors opened as the BMS protective response to the fault level reaching 3.
Same protective action, so the pack current dropped to 0 (line 28).
An escalation that followed the voltage decline.

safety_findings.statement: A 32.74 pp SOC correction not explained by measured charge. It is a pack-level estimator or measurement issue and decides nothing about which cause is right.
Three escalations were recorded with no specification to judge them against. Treat the protection as designed behaviour and request the thresholds (DOC-THRESHOLDS).

unknowns: Which of SOC estimation error, low usable capacity and current under-reading is the origin; the data cannot separate them.
Calibration and charge history before t=0 of this recording is not available.
Series count, cell chemistry, protection thresholds and the OCV curve are not available.

already_answered.answer: No. The highest cell fell 450 mV, more than the 260 mV spread at the trip, so the whole pack was depleted.
